profile.summary: Tahoe-x1 (Tx1) is a family of single-cell foundation models, up to 3 billion parameters, pretrained on single-cell transcriptomes including the Tahoe-100M drug perturbation compendium. It takes single-cell expression data (genes by Ensembl ID) and outputs cell and gene embeddings, learned jointly with compound representations, for tasks such as gene essentiality, cell-type classification and perturbation response prediction.

summary_quotes.text: a family of perturbation-trained single-cell foundation models with up to 3 billion parameters
Tx1 jointly learns representations of genes, cells, and compounds using a masked-expression generative objective that incorporates a drug token

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Tx1 is a transformer encoder pretrained with a masked-expression objective; the authors credit scGPT as inspiration for the architecture. Each gene token combines a gene embedding with a continuous expression encoding, and a CLS token gives the cell embedding. In the 3B configuration only, a chemical encoder adds a drug token (fp_dim: 2048, num_drugs: 378); the 1B and 70M configs have no chemical encoder block. The 3B configuration has 32 layers, model width 2560 and 20 heads; the 1B has 24 layers, width 2048, 16 heads; the 70M has 12 layers, width 512, 8 heads. Training uses FlashAttention on the MosaicML Composer and llm-foundry stack.

quotes.text: Transformer-based encoder pretrained with masked language modeling (MLM)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three checkpoints are released in one Hugging Face repository, in folders 70m-model, 1b-model and 3b-model, and on S3. The README calls them Tx1-70M (70M, context 1024), Tx1-1.3B (1.3B, context 2048) and Tx1-3B (3B, context 2048); the model card calls the middle one Tx1-1B with about 1.3B parameters. The README notes that the current code supports only FlashAttention without custom attention masks, while Tx1-1B and Tx1-70M were trained with the Triton backend and custom masks. A result should name the checkpoint folder, the Hugging Face revision and the repository commit.

quotes.text: The Triton backend and custom attention masks (used for training Tx1-1B and Tx1-70M) are no longer supported.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Cell and gene embeddings for cancer-relevant tasks: gene essentiality (DepMap), hallmark pathway recovery (MSigDB), cell-type classification and perturbation response prediction in held-out contexts; fine-tuning on new data.

quotes.text: (1) prediction of overall and context-specific gene essentiality, (2) identification of genes contributing to the hallmarks of cancer, (3) cell-type classification, and (4) prediction of perturbation responses in held-out cellular contexts

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Perturbation-trained single-cell foundation model family (transformer encoder, masked expression modelling).

quotes.text: a family of perturbation-trained single-cell foundation models
Transformer-based encoder pretrained with masked language modeling (MLM)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with grouped query attention (FlashAttention), pre-layer norm, continuous expression encoder and CLS cell embedding. The 3B config uses GELU, a chemical (drug) encoder and a 62721-token vocabulary; the 1B and 70M configs use ReLU, have no chemical encoder block and a 62720-token vocabulary.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An AnnData of single-cell expression with an Ensembl gene ID column; optionally a drug token from compound fingerprints.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Generating Cell and Gene Embeddings; config

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell embeddings in adata.obsm and, optionally, gene embeddings in adata.varm.

quotes.text: Cell embeddings are saved to `adata.obsm` and gene embeddings to `adata.varm` (if `return_gene_embeddings=True`).

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 3B (Tx1-3B), 1.3B (Tx1-1.3B, called Tx1-1B on the card) and 70M (Tx1-70M), as rounded by the developers. The Hugging Face API reports a safetensors total of 2,717,044,225 for the repository without saying which file it counts.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 266 million single-cell profiles from CellxGene (January 2025 release, about 61M cells), scBaseCamp (February 2025 release, about 112M) and Tahoe-100M (about 96M); filtered subsets (about 43M, 76M and 34M) were used for stage 2 of Tx1-3B.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository with uv and extract cell embeddings for an AnnData file with the Tx1-70M checkpoint downloaded from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 or newer, CUDA 12.1 or newer and an NVIDIA Ampere (A100) or newer GPU.
An h5ad file with an Ensembl gene ID column.

steps.title: Get the code and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/tahoebio/tahoe-x1.git
cd tahoe-x1
git checkout --detach 167cc19fce5888c7738b0f73f61cb4a8d3d1d457
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv venv tx1
source tx1/bin/activate
uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation-package flash-attn
steps.explanation: The README's native installation; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit. The README recommends the Docker route instead for reproducibility.
